name: code_eval
description: Execute a Python snippet to verify formulas, test algorithms, or compute results precisely. Use instead of mental arithmetic for any multi-step or nested calculation.
documentation:
Runs Python code in a restricted sandbox. Use this as a scratchpad when holding a computation in working memory would be unreliable — verify the result instead of guessing.

Ideal for:
- Verifying complex formulas before quoting a result (compound interest, physics equations, statistics)
- Testing algorithm logic with concrete inputs (sorting, recursion, searching)
- Unit conversions, ratio calculations, date arithmetic
- Validating data transformations (list reshaping, string parsing, aggregations)
- Any scenario where mental arithmetic over multiple nested steps would be error-prone

Available modules: math, statistics, json, decimal, fractions, itertools, functools, collections

Write Python. Use print() to emit results. No file I/O, no subprocess, no imports — the safe modules above are pre-loaded and ready to use.

Set 'label' to a short description of what is being computed, e.g. 'Monthly mortgage payment' or 'Fibonacci to n=20'.

trigger.description: Initiated by Chalie to verify a computation, test a formula, or validate an algorithm with concrete inputs

code.description: Python code to execute. Use print() to emit results. Available: math, statistics, json, decimal, fractions, itertools, functools, collections. No imports or file access.

label.description: Short description of what this snippet is computing, e.g. 'Compound interest at 5% for 10 years'.

output.description: Captured print() output from the snippet

error.description: Compile or runtime error, if any

tips: Always use print() — bare expressions produce no output
Use round(), decimal.Decimal, or fractions.Fraction for precise numeric output
For multi-step problems, print intermediate values to trace the computation
math, statistics, itertools, functools, collections, decimal, fractions are pre-loaded — no import needed
